stories.title: McD Defensive Playoff Failures: Another Look
stories.summary:
Apologies upfront for beating a dead horse. And just to be clear, I am 100% behind Brady, and was fully onboard with firing McDermott (not because I thought McD was a bad coach or totally at fault for our playoff failures, but because the team just needed a new voice, a breath of fresh air, some type of change, etc. to keep from falling into that "here we go again" defeatist mindset...not unlike the 90s Bills did by the 3rd and 4th Super Bowls).



	 



	 



	Now I know that many people's opinions about McDermott and the team's failures in the playoffs are pretty much set in stone. But the video/thread that ExiledInIllinois posted a while back got me thinking...and I'm just wondering what others would make of this.



	 



	I have often contended that the playoff losses were generally down to a handful of factors (in no particular order of importance/impact):



	1. Injuries. In two, maybe three years of the playoffs, our defense had suffered significant key injuries. And in the first AFC Champ game, our receivers were badly banged up.



	2. Bad luck: The Damar Hamlin situation/blizzard, bad bounces of the ball/coin tosses (literally and metaphorically), etc.



	3. The NFL/Refs (to be discussed below)



	4. Having to face the Chiefs (darlings of the NFL and a very good, multi-SB winning team) 4X in 5 years.



	5. Execution (Be that offensive turnovers in the Broncos game, or poor play on defense---13 secs, etc.)



	6. Coaching/coaching errors



	 



	But I know that there are many out there that believe, no, it was all on the coaching and the rest are just excuses. And there is also the sentiment that McDermott's defenses were good in the regular season, but fell apart/choked in the playoffs. I have previously addressed the narrative that we only feasted on bad QBs, but couldn't beat good/above-average QBs in the thread/post below (if you care to read it):



	 




	 



	And now I want to put a few pieces of data together in regards to the notion that the defense fell apart in the playoffs and see what you all think:



	 



	-In the eleven playoff games the Bills played vs. teams not named the Chiefs (in the McD era), the average points per game of our opponents was 21.81 points/game.



	-Against the Chiefs in four playoff games, K.C. averaged 34.75 points/game.



	 



	-The Bills (under McDermott) held a 6-5 record vs. the Chiefs (and Andy Reid).



	-In seven regular season match-ups vs. the Chiefs, the Bills won six of seven, and K.C. averaged 19.29 points per game in those contests.



	-In four playoff match-ups vs. the Chiefs, the Bills were 0-4, and K.C. averaged 34.75 points per game (quite a difference).



	 



	Now, some will say that it's just because the Chiefs know how to turn it up in the playoffs. Others have said, compare McDermott's regular season stats with his playoffs stats, or compare how much the Chiefs averaged in scoring during the regular season vs. McD and the Bills in the playoffs (to show that McD's defense was worse than other teams the Chiefs played, or that they fall apart in the playoffs, etc.). And those seem like reasonable arguments, but what if there is an actual factor that skews those stats a bit.



	 



	Here is the video that ExiledInIllinois posted a while back regarding which teams the refs help the most:



	 



	
		
	



	 



	What stood out to me in that video was the following: In the regular season, the Chiefs were 28th and the Bills 30th (in getting help by the refs/calls going their way), so two of the lowest teams being aided by any ref calls (pretty even)...and we usually beat the Chiefs in the regular season over the last nine years (6-1 record) and have kept them scoring below 20 points per game.



	 



	But come playoff time, the Chiefs jumped to 4th in getting help from the refs, while the Bills remained low (dead last in fact) on that list (29th) [see 14:05-14:20 in the video for reg. season compared to playoffs]. So, we still got little to no help, while the Chiefs became one of the teams most helped by the refs (in the playoffs)...and somehow K.C. won all of the playoff games against us, scoring 15-and-a-half more points per game in those 4 games over their regular season scoring average vs. the Bills (and in a smaller sample size, 4 games to 7 games).



	 



	So in the regular season (7 games), K.C. averaged 19.29 points/game against the Bills.



	In 11 playoff games not vs. K.C., our opponents averaged 21.8 points/game.



	In the regular season overall for McD's entire tenure (2017-2025; 9 years), the Bills opponents averaged 20.04 points per game



	[All seem to be pretty much in the same range, on average]



	 



	Yet in the 4 playoff games vs. the Chiefs: the Bills gave up an average of 34.75 points/game to K.C. And remember, two of those games were won by 3 points, and one went to OT. And the video only takes into account the calls that were made, not any non-calls that could have been made as well. 



	 



	I know folks don't like to blame the refs, but isn't it possible that the change in favorable calls for the Chiefs come playoff time could influence not only the outcome of games that close, but also the amount of points the Chiefs scored (and therefore how McDermott's defense is/was perceived)? Sure, we can all point to defensive coaching failures or mistakes (like 13 seconds). I'm not saying those don't exist or that McD doesn't share in the blame, nor am I saying that the refs are the sole cause of the playoff losses, but putting those points of data together, I wonder if the refs don't fall more in the direction of important factor category rather than the excuses only category regarding our playoff losses. [And you could even add in the Denver and Houston losses as well when it came to calls that affected playoff games.]



	 



	Again, not trying to beat a dead horse, just found the info in that video compelling enough to discuss. Flame away. 😉😁



	 



	 



	[Mod: ok to merge with McD thread if need be, was just curious what many posters will think of this and figured a lot of people wouldn't see it if it was buried in the McD thread.]

stories.title: Imagine an NFL Roster of Mature Adults acting like Mature Adults
stories.summary:
Bear Bryant:  “When you get in the endzone, act like you’ve been there before.”
	
	The day started watching Aidan Hutchinson injuring himself doing the now mandatory defender court jester performance. And the last afternoon games featured George Pickens with a killer taunting penalty during a comeback attempt. 
	
	It is not about being the "no fun league".  I don't care if the league enforces decorum.  I just feel like there is no creativity or novelty in the clownish behavior of most of the players, in the most trivial of circumstances.  Its become a complete bore. 
	
	I suspect that if one of the top teams actually took the tack of "acting like they had made a tackle, or a run, or reception before" and just went about their business and got set for the next play, they would actually be able to emotionally dominate the childish players.

stories.title: Calling it now...see you in LA to watch the Bills play in the Super Bowl!
stories.summary:
Getting this out there before the dawn of one of the most exciting new seasons in Bills history.  New stadium, new staff, personnel upgrades, etc - lot to be excited about.



	 



	I don't do many of these, and this is maybe my boldest calling it now with SB or bust, but I fully expect to win the division, can see 12+ wins, and I think we are and should be the favorites in the AFC today. While I have a pretty good track record on these, adding in the SB trip puts me out there a little bit on this one, but its authentically how I feel.  



	 



	Obviously the disclaimer is that is barring critical injuries...but I honestly for the first time maybe ever, really feel strongly about us representing the AFC in the Super Bowl.  I am not just saying it to say it. I have been excited for the season, optimistic, etc in the past...but something feels different this year, I really think we are going to get there.



	
		Despite online Karens feeble attempts to slander the new stadium, I think its going to prove to be a massive upgrade on home field advantage from how they engineered it for noise and the fans. 
	
	
		New HC = new energy and new ideas.  But we have the valuable benefit of CONTINUITY with the offense despite the new HC.  Yes, a frist time HC has learning curves to manage, but he has experienced support around him to help with that. More importantly to me is the offense and Allen are not having to learn new terminology, new style, new systems.  
	
	
		The offense will be top 5 again, if not the top offense in the NFL. 
		
			
				I think this is the most talented offensive group Allen has ever had collectively top to bottom - OL, RB, TE, and WR rooms combined.  
			
			
				I fully acknowledge the offense could start a little bit slow, its happened in the past and we have some personnel and staff changes to adjust to with a tough early schedule.  But come playoff time, I expect this offense will be hummng and be a real problem for teams. 
			
			
				DJ Moores impact - Not only does he give Allen his best weapons since prime Diggs, but he will make the lives and jobs easier for other playmakers like Kincaid and Shakir, not to mention allow players like Keon and Palmer to play more suitable roles rather than be forced into a more featured role.  The pass attack being able to be opened up more will also only make our elite RB room be more effective.
			
			
				BIGGET CONCERN:  Kromer retiring...but at least his philosophy stays behind as his successor has been his pupil.  And I would bet he can call Kromer for help or advice at any point if needed.
			
		
	
	
		The Defense will be more aggressive:  This is the big one for me...while a lot of new faces are on the field and the staff, I think the biggest improvement will be having a defense that can finally just go make one or two more plays in the post season that has led to us coming up short so many times. 
		
			
				We do not need them to be the 85 Bears, we just need them to not be so soft on critical downs and/or drives.  In most of our playoff losses, a single additional 3rd down stop could have flipped the outcome of those games rather than allowing a scoring drive that was the difference in those games
			
			
				BIGGEST CONCERN - A lot of new faces on the D we have not seen play together yet and several young pieces expected to play significant minutes.  
			
		
	



	I think our offense is without question going to be elite, and no one needs to go out on a limb to predict that.  But its our defense that I think will be the real difference between coming up short and getting over the hump.  I think its going to be more aggressive, less predictable, and more opportunistic.  Even just a moddest improvement in the post season could be the difference of getting over the hump, and it has the potential to be more than that.  



	 



	When I look around the AFC, I don't see a real threat staring back at me that makes me question if we can beat them.  Sure, we will lose some games during the regular season, hell we might lose week 1 like the Rams just did (the NFC darlings).  But overall for the season, I think this team proves to be amongst the elite of the league and will be a real problem for people come the post season.  
	
	GO BILLS!
